main.content: {{Npcbox | name = Zul'jin | image = Zul'jin WC2.png | gender = Male | race = Forest troll | character = Warrior | titles = Amani Warlord | affiliation = [[Amani tribe]], [[Revantusk tribe]] | faffiliation = [[Old Horde]] | faction = Horde | occupation = Axethrower, Warlord of the Amani tribe | status = Unknown }} '''Zul'jin''' (also spelled '''Zuljin'''''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' game manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Zuljin Legends of the Land]'', Zuljin) was a warlord of the [[Amani tribe|Amani]] forest trolls since before the [[Second War]]. ==Biography== ===Second War=== The feared, rogue Troll known as Zuljin had gained a great amount of notoriety over the years. Known best for his daring raids on guarded Elven villages, Zul'jin brought together many of the nomadic Troll warparties and forged them into an intimidating fighting force. The Trolls revered Zuljin and followed his leadership unconditionally. When approached by Doomhammer about joining up with the Horde, Zuljin initially declined. But with the increased tensions between the Trolls and Elves due to the coming war, Zuljin knew that only an alliance with the Orcs would save his people. During the Second War, a band of Human soldiers captured a war party led by Zul'jin and took him and his party to a secret prison near the township of [[Hillsbrad Fields|Hillsbrad]]. On Doomhammer's orders, the Horde freed Zul'jin from the prison and returned him to the trolls' own encampment nearby.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Raid_at_Hillsbrad_(WC2_Orc) Raid at Hillsbrad (WC2 Orc)] Eager to take revenge upon the humans who imprisoned them, Zul'jin and his Trolls then agreed to aid the Horde, supplying axethrowers and destroyers to the Horde war effort.[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Southshore_(WC2_Orc) Southshore (WC2 Orc)] Following the Second War, Zul'jin disappeared. Many of the Revantusk tribe hold hope that he will one day return,{{Horde}} [48] [[Cannibalistic Cousins]][[Huntsman Markhor#Quotes]] while the Hakkari believe him to be dead.Captured Hakkari Zealot says: It shall NEVER happen. We are legion. We are united. Where are your heroes? Vol'jin sits in sanctuary at the side of the young Warchief, unaware. Zul'jin missing, probably dead. ==Quotes== ===Gossip=== ... ===On-click=== ;Greeting *Hello, mon. *Ol' Zul'jin welcomes ya. *De Amani will endure. *Are ya here to help? ;Annoyed *Ya, mon? *De elves take more than me eye. *De Amani will rise again soon! *Dese were our lands... troll lands. *Zul'Aman shall not fall! *Keep that up and Zul'jin gonna cook ya! ;Farewell *May the Loa be with ya. *Take care now, mon. *Bye now. *We be meetin' again soon. ==Notes and trivia== * Prior to his initial introduction in ''Turtle WoW'' in patch 1.16, Zul'jin was mentioned several times in the game: ** Mystic Yayo'jin of the [[Revantusk|Revantusk tribe]] said: ''"If Zul'jin were here, he would have destroyed the whole lot of them with a flick of his wrist - alas, Zul'jin has not yet returned and we are left to our own devices."'' ** Huntsman Markhor of the Revantusk said: ''"Zul'jin shall return one day. Mark my words. Until then, we all hold our positions and do what we can to keep the forest troll population intact."'' ** The Captured Hakkari Zealot on Yojamba Isle said: ''"The young races? The infants? Humans? Orcs? Dwarves? You expect to defeat the Hakkari? To destroy a GOD? It shall NEVER happen. We are legion. We are united. Where are your heroes? Vol'jin sits in sanctuary at the side of the young Warchief, unaware. Zul'jin missing, probably dead." * Troll players in ''World of Warcraft'' who use the /charge emote will sometimes proclaim "For Zul'jin!" Similarly, Troll Headhunter (Warcraft III) and Troll Batrider (Warcraft III) in ''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' yell "Vengeance for Zul'jin" and "Flames for Zul'jin", respectively, despite hailing from the Darkspear tribe. * Zul'jin was removed from Turtle WoW at an unknown point. ==Patch changes== * [[File:Expansion_logo_mysteriesofazeroth.png|40px]] '''[[Patch 1.16.0]] (2021-12-27):''' Added. ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Forest troll characters]] [[Category:Amani tribe]]

Killable }} '''Zuluhed the Whacked''' is the chieftain of the [[Dragonmaw clan]]. Though he was one of the few remaining orc shamans within the [[Horde]] in Azeroth, he did not embrace his true heritage and still practiced the dark magics prescribed by [[Gul'dan]] and the [[Shadow Council]]. He and his clan were some of [[Blackhand]]'s strongest supporters during his reign as Warchief, and after his demise he honored his clan's fealty to Blackhand by pledging it into the service of the [[Black Tooth Grin clan]] led by his sons, [[Rend Blackhand|Rend]] and [[Maim Blackhand|Maim Blackhand]].''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Dragonmaw_Clan Clans of the Horde]'', Dragonmaw Clan Through unknown means, Zuluhed came into possession of what he called the [[Demon Soul]], and it is through its power that Rend and Maim masterminded the capture of the Dragon Queen, [[Alexstrasza]].''Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness'' manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_II:_Tides_of_Darkness_manual#Air_Units_of_the_Horde Air Units of the Horde]'' He entrusted the Demon Soul to [[Nekros Skullcrusher]], one of the few Warlocks who had survived [[Orgrim Doomhammer|Doomhammer]]'s purge. Meanwhile, Alexstrasza, threatened with the death of her children, unwillingly gave the Horde an endless supply of her deadly progeny.''[[Day of the Dragon]]'' When the war turned for the worse, all of Dragonmaw collected at Grim Batol, making sure that no human force could rescue the Dragon Queen. However, when Deathwing, Alextrasza's hated enemy, made a daring attempt to assassinate her, he unwittingly freed the Dragon Queen. Nekros, along with much of the Dragonmaw clan, were destroyed by Alexstrasza after she was freed. After the survivors of the Dragonmaw clan were rounded up by the Alliance and ushered into the internment camps following the battle of Grim Batol, Zuluhed disappeared in search of the remnants of the Demon Soul. He returned only when he managed to reclaim a shard of the Demon Soul from the clutches of the Red dragonflight,[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5gy_3Dy5nXE THE NEXT PATCH FOR CLASSIC+ | Turtle WoW Patch 1.18.0: Scars of the Past] claiming that it had not been destroyed by the wizard [[Rhonin]]. From the [[Dragonmaw Retreat]], Zuluhed rallied his clan, who had been freed by [[Thrall]] during the liberation of the orcs,''Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos'' game manual, ''[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Day_of_the_Dragon Orcish History]'', Day of the Dragon[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Battle_of_Grim_Batol_(History_of_Warcraft) The Battle of Grim Batol] against all those who opposed them[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0ql8IneiCk NEW CLASSIC+ DUNGEON: Dragonmaw Retreat — Turtle WoW Patch 1.18 Trailer] under the banner of the [[Dark Horde]], led by Rend. However, the Dragonmaw was not so unified, and prospective leaders such as [[Korlag Doomsong]] refused to answer Zuluhed's call due to him abandoning his clan to find the Demon Soul while the Dragonmaw fought tooth and nail for survival.{{Alliance}}{{Horde}} [35D] [[Letter from Korlag Doomsong]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Succession|Unknown|'''[[Dragonmaw clan|Chieftain of the Dragonmaw clan]]'''|Incumbent}} [[Category:Orc characters]] [[Category:Dragonmaw clan]]

'''Zul'Farrak''' is a [[Sandfury tribe|Sandfury]] troll city located in northwestern [[Tanaris]].

==History==
From the [https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Game_Guide/World_Dungeons World Dungeons] page on the official World of Warcraft Community Site:
:''This sun-blasted city is home to the Sandfury trolls, known for their particular ruthlessness and dark mysticism. Troll legends tell of a powerful sword called Sul'thraze the Lasher, a weapon capable of instilling fear and weakness in even the most formidable of foes. Long ago, the weapon was split in half. However, rumors have circulated that the two halves may be found somewhere within Zul'Farrak's walls. Reports have also suggested that a band of mercenaries fleeing Gadgetzan wandered into the city and became trapped. Their fate remains unknown. But perhaps most disturbing of all are the hushed whispers of an ancient creature sleeping within a sacred pool at the city's heart - a mighty demigod who will wreak untold destruction upon any adventurer foolish enough to awaken him.''

==History==
The nation of the [[Forest Trolls]], once the core of the great [[Amani Empire]]. Zul'Aman is a great primordial forest; the main inhabitants are the [[Forest Trolls]], however several bands of [[High Elves]] also fled into the forests after the fall of [[Quel'Thalas]]. Bands of Scourge are also present, pursuing the [[High Elves]].

==Landmarks==
Major landmarks in Zul'Aman include the capital of the [[Forest Trolls]] itself, a large pyramid called the Shrine of Ula-tek. There are also the [[Maisara Hills]], home of the [[Witch Doctor]]s of the Zul'Aman, and [[Lake Abassi]] on whose shores the [[Shrine of Ula-tek]] is built.
